checks.label: The metal feels colder because heat leaves the fingers faster: more heat arrows run from the hand into the steel than into the wood, while both thermometers read the room's temperature
At some temperature the heat leaving matches the heat being made, so the copper stops rising; at switch-on none leaves yet
The thermal resistance of the air is the surface's rise above the room divided by the losses in each metre, once the cable has settled

Every number the screens print comes from the rule: 20 W, 2 K·m/W, a 40 °C rise to 70 °C, 10 °C and 30 °C; 600 s, 10 min, 63%, 55 °C and 50 min; 4 K·m/W, 80 °C, 110 °C and 40 °C across the wrap; 1,200 s and 20 min; 0.707 and about 35 A; 30 °C, 15 W, 0.866 and about 43 A against 38 A and 80 °C; 50 °C with a fan; 55, 30 and 28 °C with 3.3 °C; 0.067 °C a second, about 4 °C a minute, against 15

Losses go with current squared (25 A makes a quarter of 50 A's 20 W); doubling the thermal resistance doubles the rise; doubling the heat capacity leaves where it settles alone and doubles the time constant

The trace follows the rule: its last point is the dot and the temperature the model returns, it never falls while the current is on, it cools back towards the room after switch-off, and it is drawn red only above 70 °C
Each puzzle offers three different answers including its right one, every wrong answer has its own hint, and before Check nothing on its picture shows the answer or a red mark

A wrong pick is drawn in red where it can be: a climb that never stops, 70 °C but later, 80 °C, settling at 50 °C, the same time, 38 A and 50 A runs, the room left out, 10 ÷ 3, 15 °C a second and all at once; a right answer draws no wrong pick

A right answer draws the rule's result: the run levels off at 70 °C; with the wrap it heads for 110 °C and turns red past the limit; twice the heat capacity also reaches 70 °C, with τ = 20 min; 43 A in a 40 °C room settles at 70 °C; the transistor at 55 °C; the first climb at 4 °C a minute
After Switch on, the copper is within 1 °C of where it settles within 3 s of the press, and its demonstration reaches that point within 3.6 s of the screen opening
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2 s
